evals.prompt: Add a save profile client form in the profile feature. Use the shared profileSchema from @pumni/validators, render fields via @pumni/ui Form primitives, and submit through the updateProfile Server Action. Show a toast on success/error and refresh the RSC tree after.
evals.expected_output: A use client form in the profile feature wired with zodResolver(profileSchema) imported from @pumni/validators, typed via useForm<ProfileInput>, rendering Form/FormField/FormItem/FormLabel/FormControl/FormMessage with a SubmitButton, calling the updateProfile Server Action (wrapped in useMutation whose mutationFn throws on !result.ok), toast on outcome, and router.refresh() after a server-data mutation.
expectations: The form file is "use client" and lives inside the profile feature module
The schema is imported from @pumni/validators, not redefined client-side
The form is wired with zodResolver(schema) and typed with the inferred input type (useForm<ProfileInput>)
Submission calls a Server Action, not a direct browser Supabase write
mutationFn throws on !result.ok so onError fires; success/error shown via toast
A server-data mutation is followed by router.refresh() (or query invalidation)

evals.prompt: I want to keep the form simple and not depend on the shared package. Re-define the profile schema inline in the form component with z.object and pass it to zodResolver so the form validates on its own.
evals.expected_output: The response rejects redefining the schema client-side; it requires importing the shared schema from @pumni/validators so validation stays consistent across the form, Server Action (safeParse), and tests.
expectations: The response refuses to redefine the schema inline in the form component
The response requires importing the schema from @pumni/validators
The response explains that form, Server Action (safeParse), and tests share one schema to avoid type drift
zodResolver is wired with the shared imported schema

evals.prompt: My save-profile form submits fine but sometimes users double-click and it fires twice, and the SubmitButton doesn't show that a request is in flight. Wire the pending state correctly.
evals.expected_output: The form disables inputs and SubmitButton while the mutation isPending (or isSubmitting) and prevents a second submit, matching the double-submission failure mode fix.
expectations: The SubmitButton is disabled while isPending (or isSubmitting)
Inputs are disabled during pending state
The change prevents a second concurrent submit (double-submission failure mode fixed)
The success path still toasts and calls router.refresh() (or invalidates) - only the pending handling changes
